name: Warehouse MHE Charging Demand Peak
trigger_conditions: tariff or demand-charge exposure remains unbounded
physical_basis: Electric MHE charging can create concentrated kW peaks without requiring extreme annual kWh.
operational_basis: Charging often clusters around shift transitions, return-to-dock windows or overnight staging.
financial_mechanism: Demand charges can make charging timing economically more material than total annual consumption.
typical_false_assumption: High electricity cost implies generic energy waste.
hypothesis: Electricity cost may be driven by MHE charging peaks rather than annual consumption intensity.
rival_hypotheses: annual consumption is the main cost driver
tariff demand is not economically material
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: charging windows overlap or shape peak demand
falsification_conditions: flat interval profile unrelated to charging windows
allowed_claim_language: MHE charging demand exposure is structurally plausible and should be falsified before annual energy use is treated as the dominant issue.
prohibited_claim_language: This warehouse has demand losses from MHE charging.
financial_exposure_if_true: energy CAPEX may target the wrong variable
tariff orchestration may matter more than generic efficiency CAPEX
retrofit economics may be overstated if demand dominates
financial_exposure_if_false: cost driver attention should shift back to alternative rival hypotheses
stop_conditions: tariff exposure bounded with bills and tariff
charging profile bounded enough to rank the hypothesis
escalation_conditions: operator charging schedule needed after public search failure
interval data requested if bills alone are insufficient
example_outputs: If charging drives peak demand, this is a tariff orchestration problem disguised as energy waste.
tests: warehouse acceptance bundle should activate this as plausible when tariff and charging are unknown
no local diagnosis language allowed without case evidence
